risks.note: Explicitly named among the key risks monitored under the Enterprise Risk Management framework. The Company counters it through a diversified customer portfolio across defence and non-defence sectors, but concentration in a high-mix, low-to-medium volume EMS model with long qualification cycles means loss of a marquee programme or OEM would be difficult to replace quickly.

Named as a key monitored risk. The Company depends on a global component supplier ecosystem; management notes geopolitical developments created short-term supply chain challenges during the year and has responded with supply chain diversification, localisation initiatives and strategic supplier partnerships.

Named as a key monitored risk. With a growing export business, increasing contribution from international customers and imported component sourcing, currency movements affect realisations and input costs; the Company cites continued focus on foreign exchange risk management and prudent treasury management.

Named as a key monitored risk. High-reliability electronics manufacturing requires continual reinvestment in advanced production equipment, inspection systems, automated testing infrastructure and Industry 4.0 capability; failure to keep pace would erode the technology-led differentiation on which the business model depends.

Named as a key monitored risk and separately flagged under Risk Management as requiring proactive management. Defence and aerospace electronics are subject to export controls and shifting trade policy, which can affect both the international expansion strategy and cross-border programme execution.

Named as a key monitored risk. currentContext.expansion: During FY 2026 Vinyas commenced the expansion of an additional 25,000 sq. ft. Class 3 manufacturing facility at its Mysuru, Karnataka base, strengthening capabilities in system integration, high-reliability manufacturing and production scalability. The Company funded this build-out from a successful preferential capital raise of ₹150 crore, whose proceeds are earmarked for advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, engineering infrastructure and future capacity expansion alongside working capital and general corporate purposes. Capability expansion also ran beyond floorspace: the Company progressively extended from PCB assembly into complex wiring harnesses, electro-mechanical assemblies, subsystem integration and system-level manufacturing, and continued investing in advanced inspection systems, automated testing infrastructure, ERP integration, real-time production monitoring and Industry 4.0-enabled digital manufacturing. Geographic expansion took the form of two wholly owned subsidiaries incorporated during the year — Vinyas Technologies Private Limited (incorporated 6 December 2025, to support capacity augmentation and focused business development in emerging market segments) and Vinyas Innovative Technologies Inc., USA (incorporated 3 February 2026, to establish North American presence; as at 31 March 2026 it had not commenced operations nor completed ODI formalities). Management reports progress towards the establishment of international operations and strategic joint ventures to support future growth, and states it remains committed to investing in capacity expansion and technology upgradation with adequate liquidity maintained for future capital expenditure requirements. No rupee capex quantum is stated as a named disclosure anywhere in this bundle.

one_liner.body: Vinyas Innovative Technologies is a Mysuru-based Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider with over three decades of experience, specialising in high-reliability electronic assemblies for defence, aerospace, medical and industrial OEMs.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: Vinyas provides end-to-end EMS solutions encompassing product industrialisation, component sourcing, Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA), box-build integration, cable harness assembly, functional testing, system integration and aftermarket support. It serves leading domestic and international OEMs across defence, aerospace, medical, industrial and other high-technology sectors on a high-mix, low-to-medium volume basis. During FY 2026 the Company expanded beyond PCB assemblies into complex wiring harnesses, electro-mechanical assemblies, subsystem integration and system-level manufacturing, …

demand_drivers.body:

- Government policy support — Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and semiconductor mission — creating opportunities for domestic electronics manufacturers

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2026 Vinyas commenced the expansion of an additional 25,000 sq. ft. Class 3 manufacturing facility at its Mysuru, Karnataka base, strengthening capabilities in system integration, high-reliability manufacturing and production scalability. The Company funded this build-out from a successful preferential capital raise of ₹150 crore, whose proceeds are earmarked for advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, engineering infrastructure and future capacity expansion alongside working capital and general corporate purposes. moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- High-reliability electronics manufacturing expertise built over three decades
- Regulated end-markets with high entry barriers — long qualification cycles and stringent customer approvals in defence and aerospace
- NADCAP AC7120 accreditation places the Company among a select group of global manufacturers meeting aerospace manufacturing standards
- Diversified customer portfolio across defence, aerospace, medical and industrial, reducing dependence on any single segment
- Long-standing relationships with leading domestic and international OEMs generating repeat business
- Vertically integrated …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Explicitly named among the key risks monitored under the Enterprise Risk Management framework. The Company counters it through a diversified customer portfolio across defence and non-defence sectors, but concentration in a high-mix, low-to-medium volume EMS model with long qualification cycles means loss of a marquee programme or OEM would be difficult to replace quickly.
- Named as a key monitored risk. The Company depends on a global component supplier ecosystem; management notes geopolitical developments created short-term supply chain challenges during the year and has responded with supply chain diversification, localisation initiatives and strategic supplier partnerships.
- Named as a key monitored risk. With a growing export business, increasing contribution from international customers and imported component sourcing, currency movements affect realisations and input costs; the Company cites continued focus on foreign exchange risk management and prudent treasury management.
- Named as a key monitored risk. High-reliability electronics manufacturing requires continual reinvestment in advanced production equipment, inspection systems, automated testing infrastructure and Industry 4.0 capability; failure to keep pace would erode the technology-led differentiation on which the business model depends.
- Named as a key monitored risk and separately flagged under Risk Management as requiring proactive management. Defence and aerospace electronics are subject to export controls and shifting trade policy, which can affect both the international expansion strategy and cross-border programme execution.
- Named as a key monitored risk. The Company's move to digital manufacturing — ERP integration, real-time production monitoring, digitised internal financial controls and AI-enabled HR systems — increases exposure, and defence and aerospace customer data carries heightened confidentiality obligations.
- Named as a key monitored risk. Operating across defence, aerospace and medical electronics subjects the Company to stringent customer-specific quality standards, regulatory qualification requirements and traceability obligations; the US subsidiary additionally awaits ODI completion under FEMA regulations.
- Management discloses that working capital remained elevated owing to higher business volumes, strategic inventory build-up, a significantly larger order book and customer-driven delivery schedules for long-cycle programmes. Sustained investment in inventory and receivables ties up capital and makes the cash conversion cycle a structural watch-item as the Company scales.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand export business and strengthen international presence, including establishing a North American footprint through Vinyas Innovative Technologies Inc., USA
- Move up the manufacturing value chain from PCBA and wiring harnesses to electro-mechanical assemblies, subsystem integration and complete system-level manufacturing
- Enhance manufacturing capacity through investment in infrastructure, advanced production equipment and a new Class 3 facility
- Accelerate automation, digitalisation and Industry 4.0 adoption — ERP integration, process automation, real-time production monitoring and …
